knowledge_statements.title: Working-Face Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polyhedral face induced by provisional active inequalities, allowing additional active constraints under degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ex=d,\ Ax\ge b\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and let \(W\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\). The associated working-face representation is \[F_W:=\{x\in P:A_Wx=b_W\}.\] If \(F_W\ne\varnothing\), then \(F_W\) is a face of \(P\). Define \(I(F_W):=\{i:A_ix=b_i\text{ for every }x\in F_W\}\). Then \(W\subseteq I(F_W)\), and the direction space parallel to \(\operatorname{aff}(F_W)\) is \[\{p\in\mathbb R^n:Ep=0,\ A_{I(F_W)}p=0\}.\] Thus provisional working constraints represent a candidate face, while additional inequalities may be active because of degeneracy or redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected inequalities imposed as equalities represent a nonempty face, but the face may have additional active inequalities. Its affine direction space is determined by the original equalities and all inequalities active throughout the face.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ex=d,\ Ax\ge b\}\) is a nonempty polyhedron with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(W\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) indexes provisional active inequalities.
\(F_W\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_W=P\cap\{x:A_Wx=b_W\}\) is a face, and its complete active-index set \(I(F_W)\) may strictly contain \(W\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual KKT Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex quadratic program with affine equality and greater-than inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ex=d,\quad Ax\ge b,\] where \(H\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(E\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and suppose the feasible set is nonempty. A feasible point \(x\) is a global minimizer if and only if there exist \(y\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(z\in\mathbb R_+^m\) such that \[Hx+c-E^Ty-A^Tz=0,\qquad z_i(A_ix-b_i)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Together with \(Ex=d\), \(Ax-b\ge0\), and \(z\ge0\), these conditions give the coupled primal-dual KKT representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex quadratic objective over a nonempty polyhedron, a feasible point is globally optimal exactly when equality and nonnegative inequality multipliers satisfy stationarity and componentwise complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(E\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
The feasible set \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ex=d,\ Ax\ge b\}\) is nonempty.
The Lagrangian is \(L(x,y,z)=\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx-y^T(Ex-d)-z^T(Ax-b)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible \(x\) is globally optimal if and only if some \((y,z)\in\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfies stationarity and complementarity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce \(s:=Ax-b\) and diagonal matrices \(S:=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\) and \(Z:=\operatorname{Diag}(z)\). The inequality part of the KKT system is then represented by \[Ax-b-s=0,\qquad s\ge0,\qquad z\ge0,\qquad SZe=0,\] where \(e\) is the all-ones vector. Exact complementarity means \(s_i z_i=0\) for every index. A primal-dual interior-point perturbation replaces the last equation by \(SZe=\mu e\) with \(\mu>0\), together with \(s>0\) and \(z>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each inequality is represented by a nonnegative slack and multiplier whose product is zero; interior-point methods replace zero products by a common positive barrier parameter.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space KKT Factorizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct symmetric-indefinite solution of a finite-dimensional equality-constrained quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the equality-constrained system \[K\begin{bmatrix}p\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\r\end{bmatrix},\qquad K:=\begin{bmatrix}H&E^T\\E&0\end{bmatrix},\] assume that \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and that \(p^THp>0\) for every nonzero \(p\in\ker E\). Then \(K\) is nonsingular. A full-space direct method selects a symmetric permutation \(P\), computes \[P^TKP=LDL^T,\] where \(L\) is unit lower triangular and \(D\) has nonsingular symmetric one-by-one or two-by-two pivot blocks, and recovers \((p,y)\) by permutation and triangular, block-diagonal, and backward substitutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-space direct method solves the nonsingular coupled KKT system using a pivoted symmetric-indefinite factorization followed by substitutions.
assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(H\in\mathbb S^n\) is positive definite on \(\ker E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT matrix \(K\) is nonsingular and can be solved through a symmetric-indefinite factorization \(P^TKP=LDL^T\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic and storage cost of the pivoted full KKT factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=n+m\) be the order of the dense KKT matrix. A dense pivoted symmetric-indefinite \(LDL^T\) factorization requires \(O(N^3)\) arithmetic and \(O(N^2)\) factor storage; each subsequent triangular and block-diagonal solve costs \(O(N^2)\). Sparse costs instead depend on ordering and fill and admit no dimension-only refinement at this leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense full-space KKT factorization is cubic in system order with quadratic factor storage; sparse costs depend on fill and ordering.
assumptions_latex: The KKT matrix is treated as dense and has order \(N=n+m\).
A stable symmetric pivoting strategy using one-by-one or two-by-two pivots is employed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{factor\ work}=O(N^3),\quad\operatorname{storage}=O(N^2),\quad\operatorname{solve\ work}=O(N^2).

children.title: Range-Space Reductions
children.top_down_role: Constraint-space elimination organized around multiplier-sized reduced systems.

assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
\(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating the primal step reduces the KKT equations to an \(m\)-dimensional range-space equation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal elimination for equality-constrained QP systems with positive-definite Hessian.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(Hp+E^Ty=-g\) and \(Ep=r\). Because \(H\) is invertible, stationarity gives \(p=-H^{-1}(g+E^Ty)\). Substitution into feasibility yields the range-space reduction \[Sy=-r-EH^{-1}g,\qquad S:=EH^{-1}E^T.\] After solving this \(m\)-dimensional system, the primal step is recovered from \(p=-H^{-1}(g+E^Ty)\). The reduction requires applications of \(H^{-1}\), normally realized by linear solves, and is especially appropriate when the number of equality constraints is smaller than the primal dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the primal step produces a multiplier system in the constraint range; solving it and one Hessian system recovers the full KKT solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space Reductions

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

assumptions_latex: Linear systems with nonsingular \(H\) can be solved without explicitly forming \(H^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(S=EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\), \(Sv=Ew\) where \(Hw=E^{\mathsf T}v\); each implicit product uses one solve with \(H\), while column assembly uses \(m\) right-hand-side solves.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free implementation and solve count for the range-space reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An implicit product with \(S=EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\) is evaluated by forming \(t=E^{\mathsf T}v\), solving \(Hw=t\), and returning \(Ew\); neither \(H^{-1}\) nor a dense Schur matrix need be formed. Explicit column assembly requires solving with \(H\) for the \(m\) columns of \(E^{\mathsf T}\), after which a factorization of \(S\) may be reused for multiple multiplier right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the range-space operator with one Hessian solve per product, or solve for all constraint right-hand sides to assemble it for reuse.
knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Range-Space Reduction

assumptions_latex: The classical range-space reduction attempts to eliminate the primal variable through \(H^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(H\) is singular, the classical formula is undefined even though the full KKT matrix may remain nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact applicability boundary of primal-block range-space elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The formula \(S=EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\) requires nonsingular \(H\). Singularity of \(H\) invalidates this classical primal-block elimination but does not imply singularity of \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&E^{\mathsf T}\\E&0\end{bmatrix}\): for \(H=[0]\) and \(E=[1]\), the KKT matrix is nonsingular. Such cases require another elimination, a null-space method, or a full-space factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular Hessian blocks classical range-space elimination but need not make the coupled KKT problem singular.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Primal-Block Boundary

children.title: Schur-Complement Systems
children.top_down_role: Reduced linear systems formed through block elimination of primal variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite range-space Schur complement of a finite-dimensional equality-constrained KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and let \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. The range-space Schur complement \[S:=EH^{-1}E^T\] belongs to \(\mathbb S_{++}^m\). Consequently, for every \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(r\in\mathbb R^m\), the system \[Sy=-r-EH^{-1}g\] has a unique solution \(y\in\mathbb R^m\). The system may be treated by a positive-definite direct factorization or by conjugate gradients using products with \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite Hessian and independent equality constraints, the range-space Schur complement is symmetric positive definite and uniquely determines the multiplier step.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
\(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=EH^{-1}E^T\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), so the Schur-complement equation has a unique multiplier solution.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
\(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) may be row-rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker(EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T})=\ker(E^{\mathsf T})\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T})=\operatorname{rank}(E)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rank and null-space structure of the Schur matrix under positive-definite primal curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S=EH^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\) with \(H\succ0\), \(y^{\mathsf T}Sy=\|H^{-1/2}E^{\mathsf T}y\|_2^2\). Consequently, \(\ker S=\ker(E^{\mathsf T})\) and \(\operatorname{rank}S=\operatorname{rank}E\). Thus \(S\) is positive definite exactly when \(E\) has full row rank; redundant equality rows make it positive semidefinite and singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive-definite H, the Schur matrix loses rank exactly when the equality matrix loses row rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Schur Rank Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Range-space Schur-complement solution of a KKT system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eliminates primal variables through a positive-definite leading block, identifies the full-row-rank condition for a positive-definite multiplier system, and records the associated block inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[K=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad G\in\mathbb{S}^n,\qquad G\succ0,\] and define \(S=AG^{-1}A^T\). Then \(S\succeq0\), and \(S\succ0\) if and only if \(A\) has full row rank. Under \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\), the KKT equations \[K\begin{bmatrix}-p\\\lambda^*\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}g\\h\end{bmatrix}\] can be solved by \[S\lambda^*=AG^{-1}g-h,\qquad Gp=A^T\lambda^*-g.\] Moreover, \[K^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}G^{-1}-G^{-1}A^TS^{-1}AG^{-1}&G^{-1}A^TS^{-1}\\S^{-1}AG^{-1}&-S^{-1}\end{bmatrix}.\] The method is especially useful when systems with \(G\) are well conditioned and inexpensive to solve, such as when \(G\) is diagonal or block diagonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite primal block G, block elimination produces S=A G-inverse A-transpose. This matrix is positive semidefinite in general and positive definite exactly when A has full row rank. In the full-row-rank case, solve the multiplier system, recover the primal step with G, and obtain the stated block inverse. The method is attractive when solves with G are easy and well conditioned.
assumptions_latex: G\in\mathbb{S}^n
G\succ0
A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}
K=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}
\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\ \text{for the unique reduced solve and inverse formula}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S:=AG^{-1}A^T\succeq0,\qquad S\succ0\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{rank}(A)=m;\qquad S\lambda^*=AG^{-1}g-h,\qquad Gp=A^T\lambda^*-g,\qquad K^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}G^{-1}-G^{-1}A^TS^{-1}AG^{-1}&G^{-1}A^TS^{-1}\\S^{-1}AG^{-1}&-S^{-1}\end{bmatrix}\ \text{when }\operatorname{rank}(A)=m.

children.title: Multiplier Recovery Regimes
children.top_down_role: Recovery quality, conditioning, and reuse considerations for multiplier-centered solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Recovery Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent multiplier-recovery procedures for an exact equality-constrained KKT step with a positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and suppose \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(Ep=r\) and \(Hp+g\in\operatorname{range}(E^T)\). A primal-first recovery computes the unique multiplier \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) from \[(EE^T)y=-E(Hp+g).\] A range-space recovery instead computes it from \[(EH^{-1}E^T)y=-r-EH^{-1}g.\] For an exact KKT step, both procedures return the same multiplier satisfying \(E^Ty=-(Hp+g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an exact KKT step with a positive-definite Hessian and independent constraints, the multiplier can be recovered either from stationarity after the primal solve or from the range-space Schur system, and the results agree.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
\(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(p\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(Ep=r\) and \(Hp+g\in\operatorname{range}(E^T)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The systems \((EE^T)y=-E(Hp+g)\) and \((EH^{-1}E^T)y=-r-EH^{-1}g\) recover the same unique multiplier for an exact KKT step.

assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
The computed primal vector \(\widehat p\) need not satisfy stationarity exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique least-squares multiplier solves \((EE^{\mathsf T})\widehat y=-E(H\widehat p+g)\), and the remaining residual is the orthogonal projection of \(H\widehat p+g\) onto \(\ker E\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier recovery and residual diagnosis for an inexact primal vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inexact primal vector \(\widehat p\), define \(\widehat y\in\arg\min_y\|H\widehat p+g+E^{\mathsf T}y\|_2\). Full row rank makes this multiplier unique, and it satisfies \((EE^{\mathsf T})\widehat y=-E(H\widehat p+g)\). The residual \(\rho=H\widehat p+g+E^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\) satisfies \(E\rho=0\) and is the component of \(H\widehat p+g\) in \(\ker E\); its norm measures stationarity error that no equality multiplier can remove.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an inexact primal solution, recover the least-squares multiplier and use the remaining null-space component as the irreducible stationarity defect.
knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Multiplier Recovery

assumptions_latex: \(E\) may be row-rank deficient.
The stationarity equation \(E^{\mathsf T}y=-w\) is considered for a specified vector \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A multiplier exists exactly when \(w\in\operatorname{range}(E^{\mathsf T})\); when one exists, all are \(y_0+\ker(E^{\mathsf T})\), and uniqueness holds exactly when \(E\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness boundary for equality-multiplier recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w=Hp+g\), the equation \(E^{\mathsf T}y=-w\) is solvable if and only if \(w\in\operatorname{range}(E^{\mathsf T})\). If \(y_0\) is one solution, every solution is \(y_0+v\) with \(v\in\ker(E^{\mathsf T})\). Thus a consistent multiplier is unique if and only if \(E\) has full row rank; redundant constraints permit distinct multipliers representing the same stationarity vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency need not prevent multiplier recovery, but it destroys uniqueness; inconsistency occurs when the stationarity vector lies outside the constraint-transpose range.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Recovery Rank Boundary

children.title: Null-Space Basis Construction
children.top_down_role: Explicit, implicit, sparse, and orthogonal representations of feasible directions.

assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank with \(m<n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A complete orthogonal factorization of \(E^T\) constructs an orthonormal basis \(Z\) of \(\ker E\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense orthogonal construction of an explicit null-space basis.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a full-row-rank matrix \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Compute a complete orthogonal factorization \[E^T=[Y\ Z]\begin{bmatrix}R\\0\end{bmatrix},\] where \([Y\ Z]\) is orthogonal, \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), and \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular upper triangular. Output \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\). It satisfies \(EZ=0\), \(Z^TZ=I\), and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker E\). Householder QR may store the orthogonal factors implicitly when explicit formation of \(Z\) is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete orthogonal factorization of the constraint transpose yields orthonormal range and null-space bases; the null-space columns are the algorithm's output.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Basis Construction

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthonormal null-space construction for possibly rank-deficient constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(E=U\Sigma V^T\) has rank \(r\), then \[Z:=V_{(:,r+1:n)}\] satisfies \(EZ=0\), \(Z^TZ=I\), and \(\operatorname{range}Z=\ker E\). In floating-point arithmetic the selected dimension depends on a numerical-rank threshold; singular values near that threshold make the computed nullity sensitive to perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Right singular vectors associated with zero singular values form an orthonormal null-space basis, including for rank-deficient constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(r<n\).
\(E=U\Sigma V^T\) is an SVD.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z=V_{(:,r+1:n)}\text{ is an orthonormal basis of }\ker E.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing SVD Construction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic construction from a nonsingular constraint column block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After a column permutation, write \(E=[E_B\ E_N]\) with \(E_B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) nonsingular. Solve \(E_BD=-E_N\) and form, in the permuted coordinates, \[N=\begin{bmatrix}D\\I_{n-m}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-E_B^{-1}E_N\\I_{n-m}\end{bmatrix}.\] Then \(EN=0\), \(N\) has full column rank, and \(\operatorname{range}N=\ker E\). The construction can exploit a sparse factorization of \(E_B\), but fails for a singular selected block and need not be orthogonal or well conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular constraint column block yields a fundamental null-space basis by solving for basic variables in terms of the remaining variables.
assumptions_latex: After a column permutation, \(E=[E_B\ E_N]\) with square nonsingular \(E_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N=\begin{bmatrix}-E_B^{-1}E_N\\I\end{bmatrix}\text{ is a full-rank basis of }\ker E.
knowledge_statements.title: Fundamental Null-Space Basis Construction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense storage and arithmetic regimes for explicit and implicit null-space representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rank \(r\), an explicit dense basis \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\) requires \(\Theta(n(n-r))\) storage. When \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank with \(m\le n\), Householder factorization of \(E^T\) costs \(O(nm^2)\), stores its reflectors in \(O(nm)\) space, and applies the represented orthogonal transformation to a vector in \(O(nm)\) work. Explicit formation of all null-space columns incurs additional work and storage, so implicit factors are preferable when nullity is large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit bases store every null-space column, whereas compact Householder factors have quadratic-in-rank construction cost and avoid nullity-sized storage.
assumptions_latex: For the QR bounds, \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and \(m\le n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{storage}(Z)=\Theta(n(n-r));\quad\operatorname{QR\ work}=O(nm^2),\quad\operatorname{reflector\ storage}=O(nm).

notation.meaning: Number of independent equality rows in the full-row-rank QR regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit and Implicit Construction Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit feasible-direction representation without explicit basis columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(E\) has full row rank, then \[P=I-E^T(EE^T)^{-1}E\] is symmetric, idempotent, satisfies \(EP=0\), and fixes every vector in \(\ker E\); hence it is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker E\). For rank-deficient \(E\), the exact extension is \(P=I-E^\dagger E\). Projector products can be computed from a factorization without forming an explicit basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unpreconditioned conjugate gradients on a finite-dimensional positive-definite null-space system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) span \(\ker E\), let \(p_0\) satisfy \(Ep_0=r\), and define \[R:=Z^THZ\in\mathbb S_{++}^{n-m},\qquad h:=-Z^T(Hp_0+g).\] Choose \(q_0\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and set \(r_0=h-Rq_0\). If \(r_0=0\), output \(p=p_0+Zq_0\). Otherwise set \(d_0=r_0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[\alpha_k=\frac{r_k^Tr_k}{d_k^TRd_k},\qquad q_{k+1}=q_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kRd_k.\] If \(\|r_{k+1}\|\le\varepsilon\|r_0\|\), output \(p=p_0+Zq_{k+1}\). Otherwise compute \[\beta_k=\frac{r_{k+1}^Tr_{k+1}}{r_k^Tr_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k,\] and continue. Every output is feasible, and with exact-arithmetic termination tolerance \(\varepsilon=0\), the method terminates in at most \(n-m\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply conjugate gradients to the positive-definite reduced Hessian, checking convergence before any potentially zero denominator, and lift the reduced iterate to a feasible primal step. Exact arithmetic requires at most the reduced dimension in iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected conjugate gradients confined to the feasible-direction space of a finite-dimensional equality-constrained quadratic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) be positive definite on \(\ker E\), and define the orthogonal projector \[P:=I-E^T(EE^T)^{-1}E.\] Given \(p_0\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(Ep_0=r\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), set \(\rho_0:=-P(Hp_0+g)\). If \(\rho_0=0\), output \(p_0\). Otherwise set \(d_0=\rho_0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[\alpha_k=\frac{\rho_k^T\rho_k}{d_k^THd_k},\qquad p_{k+1}=p_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad \rho_{k+1}=\rho_k-\alpha_kPHd_k.\] If \(\|\rho_{k+1}\|\le\varepsilon\|\rho_0\|\), output \(p_{k+1}\). Otherwise compute \[\beta_k=\frac{\rho_{k+1}^T\rho_{k+1}}{\rho_k^T\rho_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=\rho_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k,\] and continue. The corrections belong to \(\mathcal K_k(PHP,\rho_0)\subseteq\ker E\), so every iterate satisfies \(Ep_k=r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected conjugate gradients projects the stationarity residual and Hessian products into the constraint null space, updates only along feasible directions, and stops when the projected residual meets the prescribed tolerance.

children.title: Iterative Refinement
children.top_down_role: Accuracy recovery for computed QP linear-system solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-correction refinement for a computed QP linear-system solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular system \(Kz=r\), an initial computed solution \(z_0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), repeat: form the residual \(s_k=r-Kz_k\) in higher precision, approximately solve \(K d_k=s_k\) using the stored factors, and set \(z_{k+1}=z_k+d_k\). Stop when \(\lVert s_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon(\lVert K\rVert\lVert z_k\rVert+\lVert r\rVert)\), or declare stagnation if the residual no longer decreases. Return the last accepted iterate and its computed residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute residuals accurately, solve correction equations with stored factors, and update until backward error is small or refinement stagnates.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) is nonsingular.
Residual evaluation is more accurate than the correction solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful output has normwise backward error at most \(\varepsilon\).

In the dense case this is \(O(N^2)\) arithmetic per step with \(O(N^2)\) factor storage, compared with \(O(N^3)\) arithmetic for a new factorization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract convergence condition for classical or mixed-precision iterative refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_*\) solve \(Kz=r\), and let \(d_k=B(r-Kz_k)\). In exact residual arithmetic, \(\theta:=\|I-BK\|<1\) implies \(\|z_*-z_{k+1}\|\leq\theta\|z_*-z_k\|\). With finite-precision residuals, contraction persists until residual-evaluation errors dominate. A reduction by a factor \(\varepsilon\) therefore requires \(O(\log(1/\varepsilon)/|\log\theta|)\) correction solves. If \(\theta\geq1\), or residuals are not sufficiently accurate, monotone improvement is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refinement converges linearly while the reused correction solve is a contracting approximate inverse and residual errors remain small; otherwise it may stagnate or diverge.

\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(\sigma>0\), and a right-hand side \(b\) is given.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric quasi-definite primal-dual diagonal regularization and solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\delta\) so that \(B=H+\delta I\succ0\), choose \(\sigma>0\), form \(K_{\delta,\sigma}=\begin{bmatrix}B&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\sigma I\end{bmatrix}\), and solve \(K_{\delta,\sigma}z=b\) by a symmetric factorization. The multiplier-block Schur complement is \(-\sigma I-AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\prec0\); hence \(K_{\delta,\sigma}\) is symmetric quasi-definite, nonsingular, and has inertia \((n,m,0)\), without requiring full row rank of \(A\). Acceptance for the original KKT equations additionally requires testing their unregularized residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Make the primal block positive definite and the multiplier block strictly negative, solve the resulting quasi-definite system, and separately test the original KKT residual.

\((K+D)\widehat z=b\) is solved exactly for a block-diagonal regularization \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original residual is \(b-K\widehat z=D\widehat z\), so regularized-system accuracy alone does not certify accuracy for the original equations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact a posteriori measurement of regularization bias for the original KKT system.

For \(D=\operatorname{diag}(\delta I,-\sigma I)\) and \(\widehat z=(\widehat p,\widehat y)\), the residual left in the original equations is \((\delta\widehat p,-\sigma\widehat y)\). Thus a small residual for the shifted system can coexist with a large regularization bias, and acceptance for the unregularized system requires testing \(b-K\widehat z\).

Solve the regularized system, evaluate the residual for the original KKT equations, and reduce the regularization or apply refinement until the original residual tolerance is met; otherwise report regularization failure.

Then \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(R)+(m,m,0)\). Consequently, if a symmetric pivoted factorization \(PKP^{\mathsf T}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\) is computed, summing the inertias of the \(1\)-by-\(1\) and \(2\)-by-\(2\) diagonal blocks of \(D\) yields \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)\). The value \((n,m,0)\) certifies \(R\succ0\); an excess negative count or a nonzero zero count certifies negative or degenerate feasible curvature, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KKT inertia equals the reduced-Hessian inertia plus one positive and one negative eigenvalue per independent constraint; it can be extracted from the diagonal pivot blocks of a symmetric-indefinite factorization.

children.top_down_role: Boundaries where stabilization obscures or conflicts with the intended curvature regime.

assumptions_latex: \(Z^{\mathsf T}Z=I\) and \(AZ=0\).
The primal block is shifted from \(H\) to \(H+\delta I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive definiteness of the shifted reduced Hessian does not certify positive definiteness of the original reduced Hessian when the shift can mask a nonpositive eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between numerical stabilization and faithful diagnosis of original feasible curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\), the shifted reduced Hessian is \(R_\delta=Z^{\mathsf T}(H+\delta I)Z=R+\delta I\), so \(\lambda_i(R_\delta)=\lambda_i(R)+\delta\). Therefore \(R_\delta\succ0\) does not imply \(R\succ0\): if \(\lambda_{\min}(R)\leq0\) and \(\delta>-\lambda_{\min}(R)\), the shifted model is positive definite while the original has flat or negative feasible curvature. Inertia of the shifted KKT matrix consequently certifies only the shifted model unless the shift is accounted for in the spectral interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently large primal shift can make a singular or indefinite reduced Hessian appear positive definite, so shifted inertia alone cannot certify original curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Masking Boundary

assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A\).
Only the multiplier block is shifted in \(K_\sigma=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\sigma I\end{bmatrix}\).

Hence a pure dual shift may regularize multiplier coupling or rank deficiency but cannot turn zero or negative feasible primal curvature into positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-block shift changes multiplier coupling but leaves the reduced Hessian, and therefore feasible primal curvature, unchanged.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependent Constraint Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singularity caused by linearly dependent equality or working-set constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), if \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\), then there exists \(0\neq y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\). Hence \(K\begin{bmatrix}0\\y\end{bmatrix}=0\), so \(K\) is singular independently of the Hessian \(H\). Primal solutions may remain identifiable, but multipliers are nonunique: whenever \((x,\lambda)\) solves the KKT equations, so does \((x,\lambda+y)\) for every \(y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Kz=r\), with \(K\) nonsingular and \(r\ne0\), and suppose \((K+\Delta K)(z+\Delta z)=r+\Delta r\). For a consistent subordinate norm, set \(\varepsilon_K=\lVert\Delta K\rVert/\lVert K\rVert\) and \(\varepsilon_r=\lVert\Delta r\rVert/\lVert r\rVert\). If \(\kappa(K)\varepsilon_K<1\), then \[\frac{\lVert\Delta z\rVert}{\lVert z\rVert}\le \frac{\kappa(K)}{1-\kappa(K)\varepsilon_K}(\varepsilon_K+\varepsilon_r).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_W\) have full column rank and satisfy \(K_WZ_W=0\). The objective restricted to the affine working face has Hessian \(Z_W^TQZ_W\). If \(Z_W^TQZ_W\succeq0\), the restricted model is convex; if \(Z_W^TQZ_W\succ0\), its stationary point is the unique minimizer on that face. If required by the chosen interior method, apply a bounded least-squares correction to \((x^0,y^0)\) to reduce the new primal and dual residuals while retaining \(z^0,s^0>0\). Run the primal-dual method from this repaired point and stop under the ordinary scaled KKT criterion. Output the new primal-dual estimate and retain it for the next problem. Warm starting is beneficial only when the data change is sufficiently small relative to the local solution sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse the preceding primal-dual solution, repair positivity and residuals for the new data, then apply the ordinary solver and stopping test.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-QP Warm Starts

children.title: Parametric QP Tracking
children.top_down_role: Solver behavior across QPs governed by an explicit changing parameter.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tracking along a parameter path while a nonsingular active-set formula remains valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Along a path \(\theta(t)\), retain the current affine KKT formula while all inactive slacks and active multipliers remain nonnegative. Advance to the first parameter value at which an inactive slack or active multiplier reaches zero, update the candidate active set, and solve the new fixed-active-set KKT system. Simultaneous zero events require an explicit degeneracy rule; an arbitrary single update need not identify a valid adjacent region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Follow one affine solution formula to the next slack or multiplier event, then update the active set; simultaneous events require a degeneracy rule.
assumptions_latex: A continuous parameter path \(\theta(t)\) is specified.
The current active-set KKT system is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The current affine formula remains valid up to its first sign-feasibility event; tied events are an algorithmic ambiguity boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Event-to-Event Parametric Tracking

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-inclusive representation of a strictly convex affine multiparametric QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^\top Qx+(c+C\theta)^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b+B\theta\) and \(Gx\le h+H\theta\), with \(Q\succ0\). For an active set \(I\) whose KKT matrix is nonsingular, its KKT solution \((x_I(\theta),y_I(\theta),\lambda_I(\theta))\) is affine. Its closed validity region is \[\mathcal R_I=\{\theta:G_{I^c}x_I(\theta)\le h_{I^c}+H_{I^c}\theta,\ \lambda_I(\theta)\ge0\}.\] The valid regions are polyhedral and cover the feasible parameter domain. They may overlap at degenerate boundaries, but all valid formulas have the same primal component there; hence the unique optimizer \(x^*(\theta)\) is continuous and piecewise affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly convex affine parametric QP has a continuous piecewise-affine optimizer on closed polyhedral validity regions that may overlap at degenerate boundaries.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succ0\).
All problem data depend affinely on \(\theta\).
The fixed-active-set KKT system used for each formula is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible parameter domain is covered by closed polyhedral validity regions, and \(x^*(\theta)\) is continuous and piecewise affine.

notation.meaning: Closed validity region for active set I.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Critical-Region Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy-safe continuation across a tied boundary of a parameter path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a parameter \(\theta_0\), let \(E_s\) contain inactive constraints whose slacks vanish simultaneously and let \(E_\lambda\) contain active constraints whose multipliers vanish simultaneously. Form candidate outgoing active sets by adding subsets of \(E_s\) and deleting subsets of \(E_\lambda\). Retain only candidates whose KKT equations admit the required local solution and whose inactive slacks and active multipliers have the correct signs on a one-sided neighborhood in the path direction. Continue with a validated candidate; if no candidate can be validated, report tracking failure rather than applying an arbitrary single pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a tied event, test the relevant add-drop combinations and continue only with an active-set formula valid on the outgoing side.
assumptions_latex: A continuous parameter path and its outgoing direction at \(\theta_0\) are specified.
The tied event sets are finite.
Candidate formulas are accepted only after one-sided primal and dual sign validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Continuation uses a locally valid outgoing KKT regime, or tracking failure is reported.}
knowledge_statements.title: Validated Branching at Simultaneous Events

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of single-valued affine tracking when singular curvature permits multiple optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite affine-parametric convex QP with \(Q\succeq0\) singular, the fixed-active-set KKT equations may be singular and may describe an affine set of primal-dual solutions rather than one affine function of \(\theta\). The optimizer correspondence \(X^*(\theta)=\operatorname*{argmin} f_\theta\) can therefore be multivalued. The unique continuous piecewise-affine optimizer conclusion valid under \(Q\succ0\) no longer follows, and an arbitrary optimizer selection need not preserve continuity or piecewise affinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singular curvature can make the optimizer correspondence set-valued, so unique continuous piecewise-affine tracking is no longer guaranteed.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) may be singular.
The constraint system and objective data depend affinely on \(\theta\).
Only parameter values with a nonempty attained solution set are considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\succeq0\text{ alone does not guarantee a unique continuous piecewise-affine optimizer map.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-active-set representation for strictly convex multiparametric QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^\top Qx+(c+C\theta)^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b+B\theta\) and \(Gx\le h+H\theta\). For a candidate active set \(I\), solve the equality-constrained KKT equations using \(G_Ix=h_I+H_I\theta\). Nonsingularity gives \(x^*(\theta)=X_I\theta+x_I\) and affine multipliers. The parameter set on which this formula is valid is determined by the linear inequalities \(G_{I^c}x^*(\theta)<h_{I^c}+H_{I^c}\theta\) and \(z_I^*(\theta)\ge0\). Hence the feasible parameter domain is partitioned into polyhedral critical regions, and tracking consists of following the affine formula until one defining inequality becomes tight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly convex parametric QP has an affine optimizer on each polyhedral region where the valid active set remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Parametric QP Tracking

children.title: Persistent-Face Regimes
children.top_down_role: Instance sequences where active-face structure changes slowly or predictably.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nondegenerate Sufficient Condition for Face Persistence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local active-pattern stability under continuous QP perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(\bar\theta\), suppose the selected KKT point is locally unique, the active gradients are linearly independent, the active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular, every active inequality multiplier is strictly positive, and every inactive slack is strictly positive. If the QP data vary continuously, then these signs persist in a sufficiently small parameter neighborhood, so the maximal active pattern remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingularity, strict active multipliers, and strict inactive slacks ensure local persistence of the active face.
assumptions_latex: The QP data vary continuously with \(\theta\).
LICQ and active-set KKT nonsingularity hold at \(\bar\theta\).
Active multipliers and inactive slacks have positive margins at \(\bar\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(\rho>0\) such that the maximal active pattern is unchanged whenever \(\|\theta-\bar\theta\|<\rho\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nondegenerate Sufficient Condition for Face Persistence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity Does Not Imply Face Persistence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional convex-QP boundary example.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\ge0}\tfrac12(x-\theta)^2\), the unique optimizer is \(x^*(\theta)=\max\{\theta,0\}\), which is continuous. The bound is active for \(\theta<0\) and inactive for \(\theta>0\), while at \(\theta=0\) its multiplier is zero. Thus continuity of the optimizer does not imply a persistent active face, and loss of strict complementarity permits a face transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous solution max(theta,0) changes from the bound face to the interior at theta zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimizer continuity is insufficient for active-face persistence.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuity Does Not Imply Face Persistence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial persistence of an optimal face across related QPs in a fixed constraint indexing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A QP family has a persistent active-face regime at \(\bar\theta\) if there is a neighborhood \(U\) and an index set \(I\) such that a selected optimizer \(x^*(\theta)\) lies in the relative interior of the face described by exactly the maximal active pattern \(I\) for every \(\theta\in U\). This active-pattern formulation remains meaningful when the affine constraint right-hand sides vary. Continuity of \(x^*(\theta)\) alone does not imply persistence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face persists when the optimizer retains the same maximal active pattern throughout a parameter neighborhood; continuity alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The QP family uses a fixed constraint indexing and representation.
A selected optimizer exists throughout a neighborhood of \(\bar\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Face persistence is local constancy of the maximal active pattern, not merely continuity of the optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Active-Face Regime

assumptions_latex: At parameter \(\bar\theta\), the QP has a unique KKT point.
LICQ and strict complementarity hold at \(\bar\theta\).
The active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular and the data vary continuously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The same active face remains optimal throughout a sufficiently small parameter neighborhood.

notation.meaning: active set at the reference parameter

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be the active inequalities at \(x^*(\bar\theta)\). Suppose there is \(\gamma>0\) such that \(z_i^*(\bar\theta)\ge\gamma\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(h_i(\bar\theta)-G_i(\bar\theta)x^*(\bar\theta)\ge\gamma\) for every \(i\notin I\). If the active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular, its local solution depends continuously on \(\theta\). Consequently, there exists \(\rho>0\) such that, whenever \(\|\theta-\bar\theta\|<\rho\), all active multipliers remain positive and all inactive slacks remain positive. The optimal face therefore retains exactly the index set \(I\) throughout that neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive active multipliers, strictly positive inactive slacks, and a nonsingular active KKT system ensure that the optimal face persists under small parameter changes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Amortized method-selection condition for repeated QPs with reusable factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(T\) repeated QP linear systems share one nonsingular KKT matrix and only their right-hand sides change, factor once and apply the stored factors to every right-hand side. Relative to refactoring for every system, exact reuse saves \((T-1)C_f\). If matrices instead change by structured modifications, an update belongs in the reuse regime only when its construction, application, storage, and validation cost is preferable to refactorization; otherwise refactorization is the applicable route.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact same-matrix reuse amortizes one factorization across all repeated solves; changed matrices use this regime only when a validated update is cheaper than refactorization.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Reuse Regime

K_t\text{ is the current repeated-QP KKT matrix}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact numerical reuse and symbolic or updated reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Unchanged numerical factors are exact for new right-hand sides only while the coefficient matrix remains \(K\). If the current matrix is \(K_t\ne K\), even an unchanged sparsity pattern does not make the old numerical factors valid; applying them generally produces \(r_t=b_t-K_t\hat w_t\ne0\). A changed matrix therefore requires refactorization or a separately validated update. Pattern equality may justify symbolic reuse, but every returned solution is checked using the current matrix and the original QP stopping tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: New right-hand sides permit exact numerical reuse; changed coefficients require a validated update or refactorization, even when the sparsity pattern is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Current-Matrix Validation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated QPs sharing a KKT matrix or admitting stable low-rank updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every repeated QP produces the same nonsingular KKT matrix \(K\) and only the right-hand side changes, compute one factorization of \(K\); each later dense solve then costs \(O(N^2)\) arithmetic rather than another \(O(N^3)\) factorization. For sparse factors, replace these bounds by costs determined by stored factor nonzeros. If \(K\) changes by rank \(r\), a stable rank-update scheme may be used when its update cost is lower than refactorization. Reuse is admissible only while pivot quality and the residual for the current matrix remain within prescribed tolerances; otherwise the algorithm must refactorize. Thus reuse changes linear-algebra cost, not the KKT stopping requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When repeated QPs share a KKT matrix, one factorization serves many right-hand sides; changed matrices require stable updates or refactorization after residual and pivot checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Reuse Regimes

Thus the active set is identified after finitely many terms of the convergent sequence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of positive-multiplier face prediction at weakly active constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \((s^k,z^k)\to(s^*,z^*)\) and index \(i\) is weakly active, so \(s_i^*=z_i^*=0\). For every fixed \(\tau_z>0\), eventually \(z_i^k<\tau_z\); hence the rule \(s_i^k\le\tau_s^k\) and \(z_i^k\ge\tau_z\) eventually excludes \(i\). For example, the barrier points of \(\min\tfrac12x^2\) subject to \(x\ge0\) satisfy \(x(\mu)=s(\mu)=\sqrt\mu\) and \(z(\mu)=\sqrt\mu\), converging to the active constraint with zero multiplier. Exact full-active-set identification by a fixed positive multiplier threshold therefore requires a separation condition such as strict complementarity.

children.title: Interior-Point Warm-Start Limitations
children.top_down_role: Centrality and positivity difficulties when reusing boundary-near solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strictly Positive Stationary Restoration Can Be Arbitrarily Noncentral
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional QP family separating positivity and stationarity from central-neighborhood membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\ge1\), minimize \(Mx\) over \(0\le x\le1\), with slacks \(s_1=x\), \(s_2=1-x\) and lower- and upper-bound multipliers \(z_1,z_2\ge0\). The optimum is \((x,s,z)=(0,(0,1),(M,0))\). For \(0<\delta<1\), set \(x_\delta=\delta\), \(s_\delta=(\delta,1-\delta)\), and \(z_\delta=(M+\delta,\delta)\). This point is strictly primal-dual positive, primal feasible, and satisfies stationarity \(M-z_{1,\delta}+z_{2,\delta}=0\). Its complementarity products are \(\delta(M+\delta)\) and \(\delta(1-\delta)\), while \(\mu_\delta=s_\delta^{\mathsf T}z_\delta/2=\delta(M+1)/2\). Hence \[\frac{\min_i s_{i,\delta}z_{i,\delta}}{\mu_\delta}=\frac{2(1-\delta)}{M+1}\longrightarrow0\quad\text{as }M\to\infty.\] Thus positivity, primal feasibility, and stationarity do not uniformly restore centrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repaired boundary solution can be strictly positive, feasible, and stationary yet arbitrarily far from every fixed lower-product central neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{M\ge1}\frac{\min_i s_{i,\delta}z_{i,\delta}}{\mu_\delta}=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Positive Stationary Restoration Can Be Arbitrarily Noncentral

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent Positivity Floors Do Not Preserve Primal-Dual Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual obstruction when boundary slacks and multipliers are independently floored while other warm-start variables are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write inequality feasibility as \(Gx+s=h\) and stationarity as \(Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y-G^{\mathsf T}z=0\). From a feasible point, retain \(x,y\) and replace \(s,z\) by \(s+\Delta s,z+\Delta z\). The resulting residual changes are \(r_p^+=\Delta s\) and \(r_d^+=-G^{\mathsf T}\Delta z\). Thus independent positive floors generally destroy primal feasibility, dual feasibility, or both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flooring zero slacks and multipliers while retaining the other variables generally destroys primal or dual feasibility.
assumptions_latex: Gx+s=h.
Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y-G^{\mathsf T}z=0.
\Delta s\ge0,\quad\Delta z\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_p^+=\Delta s,\qquad r_d^+=-G^{\mathsf T}\Delta z.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Positivity Floors Do Not Preserve Primal-Dual Feasibility

assumptions_latex: A previous solution lies on or near the boundary, so some prior slacks or inequality multipliers are zero or extremely small.
The new problem is to be solved by a strictly feasible primal-dual interior-point method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Direct reuse can violate positivity or yield \(\min_i s_i z_i/\mu\approx0\); restoration is therefore required and may erase the anticipated warm-start benefit.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary and centrality obstruction for primal-dual interior-point warm starts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A strictly feasible primal-dual initialization requires \(s>0\) and \(z>0\), while a central-neighborhood condition additionally bounds every product \(s_i z_i\) relative to \(\mu=s^Tz/m\). A boundary-near prior solution commonly has active indices with \(s_i\approx0\) and inactive indices with \(z_i\approx0\). Reusing it unchanged violates strict positivity in the limit and can place the iterate arbitrarily far from the central path. Positive shifts and feasibility restoration repair admissibility, but sufficiently large shifts discard local information and provide no uniform iteration reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prior boundary solution is neither strictly positive nor central. Repairing its tiny slacks and multipliers may require shifts large enough to destroy the warm-start advantage.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Warm-Start Limitations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positivity and centrality obstruction is plausible, but the assertion that restoration may erase warm-start benefit and provides no uniform iteration reduction is nontrivial and uncited. A source must specify the central neighborhood and the scope of the limitation.

knowledge_statements.title: Transformation of Variable Bounds and Primal Residuals

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}Q&A_W^{\mathsf T}\\A_W&0\end{bmatrix}\), let \(x=D\widetilde x\) with nonsingular \(D\), and set \(T=\operatorname{diag}(D,I)\). Then \[\widetilde K=\begin{bmatrix}D^{\mathsf T}QD&D^{\mathsf T}A_W^{\mathsf T}\\A_WD&0\end{bmatrix}=T^{\mathsf T}KT.\] Thus rank, nullity, inertia, and nonsingularity are invariant, although numerical condition numbers need not be.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable scaling transforms a fixed-face KKT matrix by congruence, preserving exact rank and inertia but not conditioning.
assumptions_latex: Q=Q^{\mathsf T}.
D\text{ is nonsingular}.
A_W\text{ is an equality or fixed-active-set matrix}.

assumptions_latex: The QP is \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\le b\).
The diagonal scaling matrix \(D\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The substitution is bijective, preserves feasibility and objective values, and maps solutions by \(x^\star=D\tilde x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal change of variables for a quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(x=D\tilde x\). The original QP is equivalently represented as \[\min_{\tilde x}\ \tfrac12\tilde x^T(D^TQD)\tilde x+(D^Tc)^T\tilde x\quad\text{subject to}\quad (AD)\tilde x\le b.\] Because \(D\) is nonsingular, \(\tilde x\mapsto x\) is bijective, so feasibility and objective values correspond exactly. If \(Q\succeq0\), then \(D^TQD\succeq0\). Primal solutions reconstruct as \(x^\star=D\tilde x^\star\), while constraint multipliers are unchanged because the constraint functions themselves are only reparameterized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular diagonal substitution rescales variables, transforms the Hessian, linear term, and constraint columns, and preserves the QP and its convexity exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Scaling

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(q_i=a_i^Tx-b_i\), then the scaled residual is \(\widetilde q_i=r_iq_i\). The test \(|\widetilde q_i|\le\widetilde\varepsilon_i\) represents \(|q_i|\le\varepsilon_i\) exactly when \(\widetilde\varepsilon_i=r_i\varepsilon_i\). Reusing an untransformed absolute tolerance can change feasibility or activity classifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute feasibility and activity tolerances must scale with their constraint rows.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp preservation boundary for componentwise affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Multiplication of an inequality row by a positive scalar preserves it. Multiplication by a negative scalar reverses its direction, multiplication by zero destroys it, and general nonsingular mixing of inequality rows need not preserve the componentwise feasible set. Nonsingular mixing of equality rows has different semantics and is outside this leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only positive independent row scalings automatically preserve componentwise inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Admissible Inequality Row Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact geometric quantities preserved by positive diagonal constraint scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R=\operatorname{diag}(r_i)\) with \(r_i>0\), every feasible side and every zero residual is unchanged. Consequently the feasible set, active index set, faces, tangent cones, and exact row rank are unchanged, although row norms and numerical conditioning may change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row scaling preserves feasibility, activity, faces, tangent geometry, and exact rank while changing numerical magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Scaling Invariance of Active Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT-Certificate Covariance under Positive Row Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bijection between original and scaled inequality KKT certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s=b-Ax\), \(\widetilde s=R(b-Ax)=Rs\), and \(z=R\widetilde z\), where \(R=\operatorname{diag}(r_i)\) and \(r_i>0\). Then \[s\ge0\iff\widetilde s\ge0,\qquad z\ge0\iff\widetilde z\ge0,\qquad A^Tz=(RA)^T\widetilde z,\] and \[\widetilde z_i\widetilde s_i=z_is_i\quad\forall i.\] Thus primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and componentwise complementarity hold for one formulation exactly when they hold for the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled slacks and inversely scaled multiplier coordinates give a bijection between complete KKT certificates of the original and positively row-scaled inequalities.
assumptions_latex: Ax\le b
R=\operatorname{diag}(r_i)
r_i>0\ \forall i
\widetilde s=Rs
z=R\widetilde z
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{KKT}(x,s,z)\iff\operatorname{KKT}(x,\widetilde s,\widetilde z).
knowledge_statements.title: KKT-Certificate Covariance under Positive Row Scaling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Reparameterization under Positive Constraint Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariance of the inequality-constrained Lagrange dual under positive diagonal row scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax\le b\), define \[L(x,z)=f(x)+z^T(Ax-b),\qquad \widetilde L(x,\widetilde z)=f(x)+\widetilde z^TR(Ax-b).\] The bijection \(z=R\widetilde z\) maps \(\widetilde z\ge0\) onto \(z\ge0\) and gives \(\widetilde L(x,\widetilde z)=L(x,z)\). Consequently \(\widetilde g(\widetilde z)=g(R\widetilde z)\), the dual optimal values agree, and dual optimizers correspond by \(\widetilde z=R^{-1}z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row scaling reparameterizes inequality multipliers without changing the Lagrangian or dual optimal value.
assumptions_latex: R=\operatorname{diag}(r_i)
r_i>0\ \forall i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde g(\widetilde z)=g(R\widetilde z),\qquad \operatorname*{argmax}_{\widetilde z\ge0}\widetilde g=R^{-1}\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\ge0}g.

notation.meaning: Dual function for the scaled inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Reparameterization under Positive Constraint Scaling

assumptions_latex: The QP contains inequalities \(Ax\le b\).
The diagonal row-scaling matrix \(R\) has strictly positive diagonal entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The systems \(Ax\le b\) and \(RAx\le Rb\) define the same feasible set, with multipliers related by \(z=R\tilde z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal rescaling of QP constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace \(Ax\le b\) by \(RAx\le Rb\), where \(R=\operatorname{diag}(r_i)\) and every \(r_i>0\). Positivity preserves each inequality direction, hence the feasible set is unchanged. With original slack \(s=b-Ax\), the scaled slack is \(\tilde s=R(b-Ax)=Rs\). If \(\tilde z\ge0\) is the multiplier for the scaled system, equality of Lagrangian stationarity terms requires \(A^Tz=A^TR^T\tilde z\), so \(z=R\tilde z\). Complementarity is preserved componentwise up to the positive row factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying each inequality by a positive scale preserves feasibility; slacks scale with the rows, and multipliers transform inversely when reconstructing the original KKT system.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive row-scaling formulas, including scaled slacks and the multiplier relation, are internally consistent and appropriate for Constraint Scaling. However, no source with a specific locator is cited.

Sylvester's law of inertia gives \(\operatorname{inertia}(\widehat K)=\operatorname{inertia}(K)\), and rank is preserved. Independent left and right scalings generally destroy symmetry unless chosen compatibly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric matrix should be equilibrated by congruence when symmetry and inertia must be preserved.

review_flags: No asymptotic convergence claim is made when clipping remains active; the sweep cap is an explicit termination safeguard.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fully specified alternating row-column maximum-norm equilibration variant for a general sparse solver matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(R=I\), \(C=I\), and \(B=RMC\). In each sweep, for every structurally nonzero row set \(u_i=\max_j|B_{ij}|\) and update \(R\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{clip}(u_i^{-1},\ell,u))R\). Recompute \(B=RMC\); for every structurally nonzero column set \(v_j=\max_i|B_{ij}|\) and update \(C\leftarrow C\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{clip}(v_j^{-1},\ell,u))\). Leave zero rows and columns unchanged and report them. Stop after a full sweep when every scalable row and column norm \(q\) satisfies \(|\log q|\le\tau\), or after \(K\) sweeps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately normalize nonzero row and column maximum norms toward one, clip each factor, report structural zeros, and stop at logarithmic balance or a sweep limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternating Infinity-Norm Equilibration

assumptions_latex: 0<\varepsilon<1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_j|(M_\varepsilon)_{ij}|=\max_i|(M_\varepsilon)_{ij}|=1,\qquad \kappa_2(M_\varepsilon)=\frac{2-\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}\to\infty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of balanced row and column norms to certify spectral conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M_\varepsilon=\begin{bmatrix}1&1-\varepsilon\\1-\varepsilon&1\end{bmatrix}\), every row and column infinity norm equals one. Its eigenvalues are \(2-\varepsilon\) and \(\varepsilon\), so \(\kappa_2(M_\varepsilon)=(2-\varepsilon)/\varepsilon\). Hence exactly equilibrated matrices can be arbitrarily ill conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric matrix family has perfectly balanced row and column maximum norms while its spectral condition number diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Matrices Can Be Arbitrarily Ill Conditioned
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Matrices Can Be Arbitrarily Ill Conditioned

assumptions_latex: M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\text{ has no zero row or zero column}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|e_i^TRMC\|_\infty=1\ \forall i,\qquad \|RMCe_j\|_\infty=1\ \forall j.

notation.meaning: unclipped inverse row-maximum scaling followed by inverse column-maximum scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite behavior of the unclipped alternating infinity-norm variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: First scale every row of \(M\) by the reciprocal of its nonzero maximum absolute entry, obtaining \(B\). Then scale every column of \(B\) by the reciprocal of its maximum absolute entry. The resulting matrix \(RMC\) has every row and every column infinity norm equal to one. Thus the unclipped max-norm variant reaches exact balance in one row pass followed by one column pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When no row or column is zero and clipping is inactive, one row-normalization pass followed by one column-normalization pass exactly balances all maximum norms.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Max-Norm Equilibration

assumptions_latex: A matrix \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) represents a QP linear system or KKT block.
Only positive diagonal row and column scalings are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(\widehat M=RMC\) has approximately balanced nonzero row and column norms, subject to clipping and structural-zero limitations.

notation.meaning: positive diagonal row and column scalings

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative diagonal balancing of solver-system row and column magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(R=I\) and \(C=I\). At each sweep, compute nonzero row norms of \(RMC\) and multiply \(R\) by diagonal inverse norm factors; then compute nonzero column norms and update \(C\) analogously. Clip every factor to prescribed positive bounds to avoid overflow and underflow. Leave structurally zero rows or columns unchanged and report them separately. Stop when all scalable row and column norms lie within a chosen multiplicative tolerance of their target, or when a sweep limit is reached. Output \(\widehat M=RMC\) together with \(R\) and \(C\) for postsolve reversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately rescale nonzero rows and columns toward common norms, clip extreme factors, stop at balance or an iteration limit, and retain the transformations for reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Equilibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but the norm choice, target norms, update factors, clipping bounds, convergence criterion, and treatment of KKT structure define materially different equilibration variants. No citation identifies or supports the stated variant.

children.title: Structural Presolve
children.top_down_role: QP simplifications based on fixed variables, bounds, singleton structure, or removable blocks.

assumptions_latex: \ell_j\le u_j\text{ for every }j
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U(a)\le b\Rightarrow a^Tx\le b\ \forall x\in[\ell,u];\qquad L(a)>b\Rightarrow[\ell,u]\cap\{x:a^Tx\le b\}=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: minimum and maximum row activities over the current box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural certificate for a linear row over current variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\ell\le x\le u\), define \(U(a)=\sum_{a_j>0}a_ju_j+\sum_{a_j<0}a_j\ell_j\) and \(L(a)=\sum_{a_j>0}a_j\ell_j+\sum_{a_j<0}a_ju_j\), using consistent extended-real arithmetic. If \(U(a)\le b\), then \(a^Tx\le b\) is redundant over the current box. If \(L(a)>b\), the row and bounds are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interval activities can certify that a row is always satisfied or impossible under the current variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interval Certificates for Bound-Redundant and Impossible Rows
knowledge_statements.title: Interval Certificates for Bound-Redundant and Impossible Rows

assumptions_latex: \alpha\ne0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha>0\Rightarrow u_j\leftarrow\min(u_j,\beta/\alpha),\qquad \alpha<0\Rightarrow\ell_j\leftarrow\max(\ell_j,\beta/\alpha).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bound tightening from a constraint containing one unfixed variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After fixed variables are substituted, a singleton inequality \(\alpha x_j\le\beta\) with \(\alpha\ne0\) implies \(x_j\le\beta/\alpha\) for \(\alpha>0\) and \(x_j\ge\beta/\alpha\) for \(\alpha<0\). Intersecting the implication with the current bound interval is feasibility preserving; an empty intersection certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singleton row directly tightens one variable bound, with the direction determined by the coefficient sign.
knowledge_statements.title: Singleton-Row Bound Implication

assumptions_latex: Q=Q^T
x_F=v
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(v,x_R)=\tfrac12x_R^TQ_{RR}x_R+(c_R+Q_{RF}v)^Tx_R+\kappa.

notation.meaning: fixed and retained variable index sets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective and constraint transformation when structural presolve fixes variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(x=(x_F,x_R)\) and fix \(x_F=v\). With \(Q=\begin{bmatrix}Q_{FF}&Q_{FR}\\Q_{RF}&Q_{RR}\end{bmatrix}\), the reduced objective is \(\tfrac12x_R^TQ_{RR}x_R+(c_R+Q_{RF}v)^Tx_R+\kappa\), where \(\kappa=\tfrac12v^TQ_{FF}v+c_F^Tv\). A row \(A_Fx_F+A_Rx_R\le b\) becomes \(A_Rx_R\le b-A_Fv\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substituting fixed variables gives an exactly equivalent smaller QP when the induced linear term, right-hand sides, and objective offset are retained.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Fixed-Variable Elimination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative repeated application of elementary structural QP reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a queue of rows and variables affected by each accepted change. In a declared deterministic order, test contradictory bounds; classify empty rows; substitute fixed variables with the exact induced objective and right-hand-side updates; propagate singleton-row bounds; recompute interval row activities using exact arithmetic or conservative outward rounding; delete only rows certified redundant by those activities; and enqueue every affected neighbor. Retain infinite bounds symbolically. Any indeterminate floating-point comparison causes retention rather than deletion or an infeasibility declaration. Record every accepted transformation for reverse postsolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply elementary structural reductions through an affected-item queue, using conservative arithmetic and retaining numerically uncertain items.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted transformation and objective offset is logged.
Activity bounds are exact or conservatively outward-rounded.
Definitive infeasibility reports carry the corresponding contradictory-bound, empty-row, singleton, or activity certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The result is a conservatively reduced QP with a reverse log, or a verified structural infeasibility status.}
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Structural-Presolve Fixpoint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination of exact discrete presolve and the boundary for repeated numerical tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every accepted operation deletes a row, fixes or deletes a variable, or replaces a bound by a strictly stronger member of a finite candidate set. Because the model has finitely many rows and variables and each bound admits only finitely many accepted values, repeated structural presolve terminates after finitely many accepted changes. If recomputation may instead generate infinitely many distinct nominally tighter floating-point bounds, finite termination requires an additional equality-of-representation test, minimum-progress rule, or pass limit; reaching a pass limit is not an exact fixpoint unless the declared stopping rule defines it as such.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite discrete deletions and finite-set bound updates terminate; unrestricted repeated numerical tightening needs an explicit stopping rule.
assumptions_latex: Accepted bound changes are monotone.
For unconditional finite termination, accepted bound values belong to finite candidate sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Finite model size and finite monotone update sets imply finite termination.}
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Termination Boundary for Structural Presolve

assumptions_latex: The finite-dimensional QP is represented by explicit bounds, linear constraints, and a quadratic objective.
Every transformation records sufficient data for exact reversal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced QP is infeasible exactly when a sound presolve check proves inconsistency; otherwise its solutions reconstruct to solutions of the unreduced QP.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reversible structural reductions applied before numerical QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an empty transformation log \(\mathcal T\). Repeatedly remove empty rows, detect inconsistent constant rows, fix variables whose lower and upper bounds coincide, substitute fixed variables into the objective and constraints, tighten bounds using singleton rows, and delete constraints made redundant by current bounds. Record each substitution, deletion, objective-offset change, and scaling in \(\mathcal T\). Continue until a complete sweep makes no change. If a sound check finds contradictory bounds or an impossible row, output an infeasibility certificate; otherwise output the reduced QP and \(\mathcal T\), which must support reverse-order postsolve reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly eliminate empty structure, fixed variables, singleton implications, and bound-redundant rows while logging every reversible transformation and detecting explicit inconsistencies.
knowledge_statements.title: Structural Presolve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed presolve catalog and reversibility requirement fit the container, but soundness of bound tightening, redundancy deletion, infeasibility detection, and postsolve logging is nontrivial and uncited. The form of the promised infeasibility certificate is also unspecified.

children.top_down_role: Identification of constraints that do not alter the feasible region or relevant face structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_i^T\bar x>b_i\Rightarrow P_{-i}\supsetneq P_{-i}\cap\{x:a_i^Tx\le b_i\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal disproof of global redundancy for one represented affine inequality.

\sup_{x\in P_{-i}}a_i^Tx<+\infty\text{ for the converse}

Let \(P_{-i}=\{x:A_{-i}x\le b_{-i},\ Ex=f\}\) be nonempty. If \(\lambda\ge0\) and unrestricted \(
u\) satisfy \(A_{-i}^T\lambda+E^T
u=a_i\) and \(b_{-i}^T\lambda+f^T
u\le b_i\), then \(a_i^Tx\le b_i\) is valid on \(P_{-i}\). Conversely, when the auxiliary linear maximization has a finite optimum, LP strong duality yields such multipliers for every valid candidate row.

If the optimum is finite and \(\rho_i\le b_i\), report redundancy with a verified dual implication certificate. If it is finite and \(\rho_i>b_i\), report nonredundancy with a violating feasible point. If the auxiliary problem is unbounded above, a feasible point with \(a_i^Tx>b_i\), obtainable along the certified improving ray from a feasible base point, certifies nonredundancy. Every definitive status is accompanied by the corresponding primal or dual LP certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Each certified outcome maps to redundancy, nonredundancy, or remainder infeasibility; otherwise the result is unknown.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic computational structure of optimization-based redundancy detection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\) candidate inequalities, an independent complete scan solves at most \(m\) auxiliary linear programs, each using the common equality system and all inequalities except its candidate row. Using a polynomial-time LP algorithm yields polynomial total worst-case complexity in the encoded input size and \(m\). Warm starts, common bases, and incremental factorizations may reduce practical work, but without an additional simultaneous-redundancy argument they do not improve the worst-case count of candidate tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct scan uses one auxiliary LP per candidate row; shared solver state improves practice but does not change that worst-case test count.
assumptions_latex: There are \(m\) represented candidate inequalities.
Each auxiliary LP is solved to a certificate-backed status by a polynomial-time LP method for the stated complexity conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{LP}}\le m.

notation.meaning: Number of auxiliary LP solves in an independent full scan.

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Row LP Complexity and Reuse Boundary

assumptions_latex: The candidate inequality is \(a_i^Tx\le b_i\).
The remaining constraints define a nonempty set \(P_{-i}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\rho_i\le b_i\), the candidate constraint is redundant; any valid upper bound \(U_i\le b_i\) also certifies redundancy.

notation.meaning: feasible region without the candidate row
certified upper bound on the test value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-based certificate for redundancy of one linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Remove row \(i\) and define \(P_{-i}=\{x:a_j^Tx\le b_j\text{ for }j\ne i\}\). Compute or validly upper-bound \(\rho_i=\sup\{a_i^Tx:x\in P_{-i}\}\). If a finite certified bound \(U_i\) satisfies \(\rho_i\le U_i\le b_i\), then every point feasible for the remaining constraints satisfies row \(i\), so the row is redundant. A dual-feasible solution of the linear maximization problem whose objective value is at most \(b_i\) is a directly checkable certificate. If \(\rho_i>b_i\), a maximizing feasible point certifies nonredundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize a candidate row's left side over all other constraints. An upper bound no larger than its right side certifies redundancy; a violating feasible point disproves it.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Constraint Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimization-based redundancy test is mathematically plausible and the certificate content kind fits. An authoritative source is still required, and the claimed dual certificate must explicitly state the dual problem and the assumptions ensuring weak-duality validity and bounded certification.

A\text{ is represented in finite precision}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}_\tau(RA)\text{ need not equal }\operatorname{rank}_\tau(A)\text{ for a nonsingular diagonal }R.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact row dependence and tolerance-dependent numerical cleanup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact rank is invariant under nonsingular row scaling, but \(\operatorname{rank}_\tau(A)=|\{k:\sigma_k(A)>\tau\}|\) generally is not. Numerical deletion therefore requires a declared scaling, norm, rank threshold, and separate right-hand-side consistency bound; a small singular value alone does not certify exact redundancy.
