knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical Rank Is Scale and Tolerance Dependent
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Rank Is Scale and Tolerance Dependent

assumptions_latex: A=TA_I
b=Tb_I
\operatorname{rank}(A_I)=|I|
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:Ax=b\}=\{x:A_Ix=b_I\},\qquad T^T\mu=\mu_I\Rightarrow A^T\mu=A_I^T\mu_I.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence and dual reconstruction after deleting dependent, consistent equality or working-set rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(A=TA_I\) and \(b=Tb_I\), where \(A_I\) has full row rank. Then \(Ax=b\) if and only if \(A_Ix=b_I\). Every reduced multiplier \(\mu_I\) has at least one full representation \(\mu\) satisfying \(T^T\mu=\mu_I\), and then \(A^T\mu=A_I^T\mu_I\); the full multiplier generally is not unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting exactly dependent rows with consistent right-hand sides preserves the feasible set, and reduced multiplier contributions can be lifted through the dependence matrix, generally nonuniquely.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Row Reduction and Multiplier Reconstruction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative numerical classification of dependent equality or working-set rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Scale rows and right-hand sides by declared positive factors, compute a rank-revealing QR or SVD, and select candidate retained rows \(I\). For an omitted row, compute coefficients \(t_j\) and normalized residuals \[r_{a,j}=\frac{\|a_j-t_j^TA_I\|}{\|a_j\|+\|t_j^TA_I\|+\delta},\qquad r_{b,j}=\frac{|b_j-t_j^Tb_I|}{|b_j|+|t_j^Tb_I|+\delta}.\] Exact deletion is justified only by an exact or independently verified dependence relation. Under a declared numerical policy, a row may instead be labeled numerically dependent and consistent when both residuals pass their respective acceptance thresholds. If the row residual passes but the right-hand-side residual does not, generate an inconsistency witness for independent verification; absent such verification, report numerical inconsistency or uncertainty rather than exact infeasibility. Borderline cases are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use separate scaled row-span and right-hand-side tests, and distinguish exact deletion, tolerance-based cleanup, verified infeasibility, and uncertainty.
assumptions_latex: Declared row scaling, norm, \(\delta>0\), and separate residual thresholds are supplied.
Tolerance-based deletion is identified as a numerical model modification unless exact dependence is independently verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No borderline or merely approximate dependence test is reported as exact redundancy or exact infeasibility.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-controlled removal of dependent QP constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply a rank-revealing QR or singular-value decomposition to \(A_W^T\) and determine a numerical rank \(r\) using tolerance \(\tau\). Select independent row indices \(I\) of cardinality \(r\). For each omitted row, compute coefficients expressing it in the span of \(A_I\) and check the corresponding right-hand-side relation. If the row residual is at most \(\tau\) and the right-hand side is consistent, delete the row and log its dependence coefficients. If the coefficient relation holds but the right-hand side is inconsistent, report infeasibility. Output the cleaned system and reconstruction log.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a rank-revealing factorization to retain independent rows, delete consistent dependent rows with logged coefficients, and declare infeasibility when a dependent left side has an inconsistent right side.

children.title: Solution Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original primal variables after presolve transformations or eliminations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic reversal and validation of presolve transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with the reduced solution and traverse the presolve log in reverse order. Apply each recorded inverse or lifting operation to restore fixed, substituted, scaled, and permuted variables and to accumulate the recorded objective offset. After reconstruction, verify every original bound and constraint and the objective-offset identity. If an operation lacks the data required by its reconstruction invariant or a verification test fails, report reconstruction failure rather than an original solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse the presolve log, restore all original variables, and validate original feasibility and the objective offset.
assumptions_latex: The presolve log records a valid lifting and validation invariant for every transformation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The result is either a validated original primal point or explicit reconstruction failure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality transfer through a feasible-set lifting and constant objective offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar{\mathcal F}\) and \(\mathcal F\) be the reduced and original feasible sets. If the recorded map \(R\) satisfies \(R(\bar{\mathcal F})=\mathcal F\) and \(f(R(z))=\bar f(z)+\gamma\) for every \(z\in\bar{\mathcal F}\), then every \(\bar z\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\bar{\mathcal F}}\bar f(z)\) reconstructs to \(R(\bar z)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal F}f(x)\), with \(f^*=\bar f^*+\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced optimizer lifts to an original optimizer when the reconstruction covers the original feasible set and preserves objective values up to a constant.
assumptions_latex: \(R(\bar{\mathcal F})=\mathcal F\).
\(f(R(z))=\bar f(z)+\gamma\) throughout the reduced feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(\bar z)\) is an original minimizer and \(f^*=\bar f^*+\gamma\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coordinate lifting for common reversible presolve transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variable permutation is reversed by its inverse permutation. A recorded affine scaling \(x=Dz+d\), with nonsingular diagonal \(D\), is reversed by that affine map. A fixed variable is restored at its recorded value, and an eliminated variable satisfying \(x_j=\alpha+q^Tz\) is restored from that recorded defining equation. Composing the elementary liftings in reverse presolve order gives the full primal reconstruction map \(R\). If an operation omits a required index, coefficient, scale, offset, or defining relation, exact reconstruction through that operation is undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Undo permutations, affine scalings, fixed variables, and affine substitutions with their recorded maps in reverse presolve order.
assumptions_latex: Every eliminated coordinate has a recorded exact defining relation.
Every variable scaling retains its nonsingular scale and offset.
The operation order is retained.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic postsolve recovery of original equality and inequality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reverse the recorded dual effects of presolve transformations in reverse order, retaining mapped multipliers for surviving rows and solving for missing components subject to original-space stationarity. Set multipliers of constraints verified strictly inactive to zero and enforce nonnegativity on inequality multipliers. Accept a reconstructed pair only when original-space stationarity, multiplier-sign, and complementarity residuals meet declared tolerances; otherwise report multiplier-reconstruction failure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a KKT-consistent original multiplier pair or an explicit reconstruction failure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity transport and information loss under affine primal elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(x=Tz+d\), the reduced stationarity residual is \(r_z=T^{\mathsf T}r_x\), where \(r_x=Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}\lambda\). Thus original stationarity implies reduced stationarity. If \(T\) is not surjective, \(T^{\mathsf T}r_x=0\) permits nonzero \(r_x\in\ker(T^{\mathsf T})\), so reduced stationarity need not determine eliminated multiplier components or certify original stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced stationarity is the adjoint pullback of original stationarity and can hide residual components introduced by elimination.
assumptions_latex: Original variables satisfy the affine reconstruction map \(x=Tz+d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Original multipliers must be reconstructed and checked in original space whenever \(T^{\mathsf T}\) loses information.
knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint Stationarity Map

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Multiplier Map for Row Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse dual map for elementary equality and inequality row scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an equality residual \(a^Tx-b=0\) is replaced by \(\alpha(a^Tx-b)=0\), where \(\alpha\ne0\), its transformed multiplier \(\bar y\) maps to the original multiplier \(y=\alpha\bar y\). If an inequality residual \(a^Tx-b\le0\) is replaced by \(\alpha(a^Tx-b)\le0\), where \(\alpha>0\), its transformed multiplier maps as \(\lambda=\alpha\bar\lambda\). These maps preserve the row's stationarity contribution, and the positive inequality scaling also preserves multiplier sign and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row scaled by alpha has its transformed multiplier multiplied by alpha when mapped back to the original row.
assumptions_latex: Equality scaling uses \(\alpha\ne0\).
Inequality scaling uses \(\alpha>0\) and retains the same residual convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y=\alpha\bar y\quad\text{or}\quad\lambda=\alpha\bar\lambda.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Multiplier Map for Row Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact original-space recovery for an eliminated equality block once all other stationarity contributions are known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the eliminated equalities be \(Cx=d\), where \(C\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) has full row rank, and let \(r=Qx+c+B^{\mathsf T}\nu+G^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) collect every stationarity contribution except \(C^{\mathsf T}y\). An exact original equality multiplier exists if and only if \(r\in\operatorname{range}(C^{\mathsf T})\). In that case it is unique and equals \[y=-(CC^{\mathsf T})^{-1}Cr.\] Reject the reconstruction when the original-space residual \(r+C^{\mathsf T}y\) exceeds its declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an eliminated independent equality block, recover its multiplier from the row-space stationarity equation and verify the result in original space.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) has full row rank.
The primal point and every stationarity contribution not associated with \(C\) have already been reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r\in\operatorname{range}(C^{\mathsf T})\Longrightarrow y=-(CC^{\mathsf T})^{-1}Cr\ \text{and}\ r+C^{\mathsf T}y=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be the reconstructed original feasible point for \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), let \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i:G_ix=h_i\}\), and let \(r_0\) contain the objective gradient and every already reconstructed stationarity contribution. Otherwise select a declared deterministic member, for example the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm element, and accept it only after original-space stationarity, sign, and complementarity residual checks.

Tolerance-Sensitive Solver Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity caused by residuals lying near user-selected feasibility, activity, or optimality thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_p,r_d,r_c\ge0\) denote scaled primal-feasibility, dual-feasibility, and complementarity residuals, and let \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_c>0\) be their acceptance tolerances. The status predicate
\[
\mathrm{AcceptOptimal}\iff r_p\le\varepsilon_p,\quad r_d\le\varepsilon_d,\quad r_c\le\varepsilon_c
\]
is not robust when any margin \(\lvert r_j-\varepsilon_j\rvert\) is comparable to residual-evaluation error \(\eta_j\). If \(\lvert r_j-\varepsilon_j\rvert\le\eta_j\) for some \(j\), two admissible evaluations can place the same iterate on opposite sides of the test. The solver must therefore report a tolerance-sensitive or indeterminate status unless directed rounding or certified residual bounds decide every predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A definitive status is unsafe when residual uncertainty overlaps a feasibility, duality, complementarity, or activity threshold; certified bounds or an indeterminate status are then required.
assumptions_latex: Each computed residual \(\widehat r_j\) satisfies \(\lvert \widehat r_j-r_j\rvert\le\eta_j\).
Status acceptance is defined by componentwise residual thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever a residual uncertainty interval intersects its threshold, the corresponding Boolean status test is numerically ambiguous.

notation.meaning: User-selected acceptance threshold for residual class j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: threshold instability under bounded residual error follows directly from interval overlap

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the terminal topic, and interval overlap does explain a tolerance-sensitive Boolean test. The plain statement additionally mentions activity thresholds, which are absent from the formal residual predicate. More importantly, the mandatory policy of reporting an indeterminate status is not established by a cited solver standard or numerical-analysis source. A specific authoritative locator is required before choosing the exact formulation.

children.title: Downstream QP Solver Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interface requirements imposed by larger optimization, control, and discrete-search systems without importing their internal theory.

children.title: Repeated QP Subproblem Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Warm-start, accuracy, and status interfaces for repeated local-model QPs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound status semantics for budget-limited repeated convex-QP calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the solver exhausts \(B_k\) before producing residuals that certify optimality or a separately verifiable infeasibility or unboundedness certificate, it must return a noncertifying status such as \(\mathrm{limit}\) or \(\mathrm{unknown}\). Warm-start state and failure to find a feasible point within \(B_k\) do not satisfy an infeasibility predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Budget exhaustion without a certificate must produce an unknown or limit status, not a mathematical claim of optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: Each terminal status has a fixed predicate over the current call's original QP data.
Warm state may change computation but not those predicates.
The work budget may expire before a terminal predicate is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_k\text{ exhausted without certification}\implies s_k\in\{\mathrm{limit},\mathrm{unknown}\}.

notation.meaning: work or time budget for call k

knowledge_statements.title: Budget-Limited Status Soundness
Repeated QP Subproblem Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A mathematical input-output contract for sequentially related convex QP solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At call \(k\), represent the subproblem interface by
\[
\mathcal I_k=(Q_k,c_k,A_k,b_k,G_k,h_k,w_{k-1},\tau_k,B_k),
\]
where \(w_{k-1}\) is optional primal-dual-active-set state, \(\tau_k\) specifies residual tolerances, and \(B_k\) is a work or time budget. The solver returns \(\mathcal O_k=(x_k,y_k,\lambda_k,W_k,s_k,r_k)\), where \(s_k\) is a status and \(r_k\) contains original-data residuals. A warm start may affect computation but not the status predicate: any optimal status requires \(r_k\le\tau_k\), and any infeasible or unbounded status requires a separately checkable certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each repeated call carries QP data, optional prior state, tolerances, and a budget, and returns a solution state, status, and independently checkable residuals or certificate.
assumptions_latex: Each \(Q_k\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.
Dimensions and row identities are supplied consistently across each call.
Residual scaling and the interpretation of every status are fixed by the interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tuple \(\mathcal I_k\mapsto\mathcal O_k\) separates reusable computational state from tolerance-governed mathematical certification.

notation.meaning: Optional warm-start state inherited from the preceding solve.
Reported status and verification residual vector.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: repeated-solve interfaces conventionally separate problem data, warm state, tolerances, budgets, and certified outputs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A representation is appropriate for this interface leaf, but the proposed tuple is an uncited design contract rather than a sourced standard. The output component W_k is not introduced, the componentwise or norm meaning of r_k\le\tau_k is unspecified, and no certificate object appears in the output tuple despite the requirement for separately checkable infeasibility or unboundedness evidence. An authoritative repeated-QP interface source is needed to determine the correct contract.

children.title: Structured Control-QP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Structure and latency interfaces for receding-horizon QP workloads.

assumptions_latex: Successive calls may change the measured state, disturbances, bounds, stage data, or terminal data.
A latency budget and output-verification tolerances are declared by the caller.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_k\in\mathcal F_k\centernot\implies\operatorname{shift}(U_k)\in\mathcal F_{k+1};\quad\text{deadline termination asserts only separately verified properties}.

notation.meaning: Feasible control-sequence set at sampling instant k.
Control sequence obtained by dropping the first control and appending a terminal control.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start and deadline semantics across successive receding-horizon QP calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A repeated-call interface may accept shifted primal-dual stage variables and compatible factorization metadata, but a previously feasible trajectory or its shifted control sequence is only an initialization for the new QP. Changed measurements, disturbances, constraints, or terminal extension can make it infeasible. On deadline termination, the interface reports elapsed work, achieved residuals, and only those controls, bounds, or statuses that have been independently checked against the current stage model; an unchecked iterate is not a feasible-control certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shifted trajectories are warm starts rather than feasibility certificates, and deadline outputs may claim only properties verified for the current horizon problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Call and Deadline Semantics

assumptions_latex: x_{i+1}=A_i x_i+B_i u_i+c_i\quad(i=0,\ldots,N-1)
x_0=\bar x
The eliminated states are uniquely determined by \((\bar x,U)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X=\mathcal A\bar x+\mathcal B U+\mathcal c,\qquad \operatorname{proj}_U(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{sparse}})=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{condensed}}.

notation.meaning: Prediction operators obtained by recursive dynamics substitution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent solver-facing representations of a finite-horizon convex control QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For linear dynamics \(x_{i+1}=A_i x_i+B_i u_i+c_i\) and fixed measured state \(x_0=\bar x\), a sparse interface retains predicted states and controls, block-banded dynamics equalities, stage costs and constraints, and the terminal cost and constraints. Recursive substitution gives \(X=\mathcal A\bar x+\mathcal B U+\mathcal c\) and an input-condensed QP. Exact substitution makes the formulations equivalent under projection onto \(U\), although condensation can turn stage-local sparse Hessian and constraint blocks into dense blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A control QP can expose sparse stage variables and dynamics or an exactly condensed input-only model; the feasible controls agree, but the linear-algebra structure can differ substantially.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse and Condensed Control-QP Interfaces
Structured Control-QP Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A horizon-structured interface for latency-constrained receding-horizon convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For horizon \(N\), expose stage data \((Q_i,q_i,A_i,B_i,c_i)\), convex stage constraints \(C_i z_i\le d_i\), terminal data, and the measured initial state \(x_0=\bar x\), rather than only a fully assembled dense QP. The interface returns a control sequence, primal-dual stage variables, residuals, status, and elapsed work. Between sampling instants it may accept shifted stage variables and factorization metadata as a warm start. Any deadline-terminated output must distinguish a certified feasible incumbent from an unchecked iterate, and any optimal status must satisfy the requested original-stage residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expose horizon stage structure, the current state, warm-start metadata, tolerances, and deadlines; return stagewise variables with status and certification appropriate to the completed work.
assumptions_latex: The finite-horizon control problem is a convex QP with linear dynamics.
Stage ordering and sparsity identities remain defined across calls.
The caller supplies residual tolerances and any hard latency budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structured interface preserves stagewise sparsity while making feasibility, optimality, and deadline termination distinguishable and checkable.

notation.meaning: Initial-state equality imposed at the current sampling instant.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stagewise data, shifted warm starts, deadlines, and residual-bearing outputs are standard control-QP interface elements

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Structured Control-QP Interfaces, but the mathematical interface is incomplete: z_i and the relationship of A_i,B_i,c_i to the linear dynamics are not defined, and terminal data are only named. The deadline and certification requirements are also uncited design prescriptions. A specific MPC or control-QP interface source is required to fix the stage model and supported outputs.

children.title: Search-Tree QP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Warm-start and certificate interfaces for convex QP relaxations at search nodes.

children.title: Branching-Node QP Inputs
children.top_down_role: QP relaxation data passed from a search node to the convex solver.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parent-child consistency condition for branching-node QP inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_v\) and \(F_w\) be the relaxation feasible regions encoded by parent input \(v\) and child input \(w\). If the child retains the same objective and inherited global rows and changes the model only through valid bound tightening or added node constraints, then a valid child input must satisfy \(F_w\subseteq F_v\). Consequently, for minimization, \(\inf_{x\in F_w}f(x)\ge\inf_{x\in F_v}f(x)\) in the extended real numbers. Without the inclusion, parent-bound inheritance cannot be inferred.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid child-node input restricts its parent's relaxation, so its minimization relaxation value cannot improve downward.
assumptions_latex: Parent and child use the same extended-real objective \(f\).
The child retains inherited model rows and adds only valid restrictions.
Both nodes use the minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_w\subseteq F_v\quad\text{and hence}\quad\inf_{x\in F_w}f(x)\ge\inf_{x\in F_v}f(x).

notation.meaning: parent and child relaxation feasible regions

knowledge_statements.title: Valid Child-Input Restriction
Branching-Node QP Inputs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convex-QP data passed from a search-tree node to its relaxation solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For node \(v\), define the relaxation input as
\[
\mathcal I_v=(Q,c,A,b,G,h,\ell^v,u^v,\mathcal C_v,w_{ar v},U,\tau),
\]
where \((\ell^v,u^v)\) are node bounds, \(\mathcal C_v\) are locally added valid constraints, \(w_{ar v}\) is optional parent state, \(U\) is the incumbent cutoff, and \(\tau\) specifies certification tolerances. The node relaxation is the convex QP over \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), \(\ell^v\le x\le u^v\), and \(x\in\mathcal C_v\). Every row and bound carries a stable identifier so returned multipliers and certificates can be associated with the node model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching node supplies global QP data, local bounds and cuts, parent warm state, incumbent cutoff, tolerances, and stable row identities.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
The node bounds and local constraints define a valid relaxation of the node's discrete subproblem.
The incumbent cutoff \(U\) uses the minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tuple \(\mathcal I_v\) uniquely specifies the node relaxation and the metadata required for warm starts and certificate attribution.

notation.meaning: Current search-tree node and its parent.
Objective value of the current feasible incumbent.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: branch-and-bound node relaxations are determined by inherited model data, local domain restrictions, cut data, and search metadata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A representation fits the Branching-Node QP Inputs leaf, but the cited inventory does not support this QP interface tuple and source_refs is empty. The symbol w_{ar v} is inconsistent with the notation entry referring to parent \bar v, while \mathcal C_v is described as a collection of constraints but used as a feasible set in x\in\mathcal C_v. The claim that the tuple uniquely specifies the relaxation also requires explicit definitions of the local constraints and objective conventions.

children.title: Bound Certification Outputs
children.top_down_role: Solver outputs used to establish node bounds or relaxation infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable infeasibility output for the affine constraints of a convex-QP node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), if \(y\) and \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfy \(A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}\lambda<0\), then the constraint system is infeasible. The output is certifying only when these conditions hold exactly or through rigorous residual and strict-negativity enclosures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Farkas multiplier vector with zero combined normal and a strictly negative combined right-hand side certifies node-relaxation infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The node constraints are \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\).
The equalities, nonnegativity, and strict inequality are verified exactly or by rigorous enclosures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Relaxation Infeasibility Certificate
Bound Certification Outputs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable lower-bound outputs from a convex QP relaxation at a minimization search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For node relaxation \(\min_x \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), a dual-feasible pair \((y,\lambda)\) with \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}\lambda\in\operatorname{Range}(Q)\) certifies the lower bound
\[
L=-b^{\mathsf T}y-h^{\mathsf T}\lambda-	frac12 q^{\mathsf T}Q^{\dagger}q,
\qquad q=c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}\lambda.
\]
The output must include \(L\), the multipliers, and residual bounds sufficient to verify the sign and range conditions. A node may be pruned against incumbent \(U\) only when the certified inequality \(L\ge U\) remains valid after numerical error is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-feasible multipliers certify a node lower bound; pruning is valid only when residual-aware verification proves that bound is at least the incumbent value.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
The node relaxation is a minimization problem with affine equality and inequality constraints.
Numerical residuals are enclosed by explicit verification bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible node point has objective value at least \(L\), and \(L\ge U\) certifies bound-based pruning.

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the positive-semidefinite Hessian.
Certified dual lower bound for the node relaxation.
Objective value of a feasible incumbent.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed value is the Lagrangian dual function of a convex QP evaluated at dual-feasible multipliers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind is correct for this leaf, and the displayed Lagrangian dual value has the correct sign convention for Gx\le h with \lambda\ge0. Nevertheless, no authoritative convex-QP duality locator is supplied. The record also needs a sourced, precise account of how numerical evidence certifies membership of q in Range(Q), especially when Q is singular, before the residual-aware pruning claim is reliable.

children.title: Search-Tree Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reusable solver state exchanged across related nodes in the search tree.

assumptions_latex: The child feasible set \(X_v\) may be a proper subset of the parent feasible set \(X_p\).
The solver has a cold initialization and current-child admission and termination tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_p\in X_p\centernot\implies x_p\in X_v,\qquad \operatorname{Verify}_{P_v}(w,\sigma)\text{ is required independently of initialization}.

notation.meaning: Mapped candidate initialization for the child.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent admission and fallback procedure for a child-node warm start.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Map the reusable parent state to a candidate child state \(w_v^0\), invalidate components affected by changed rows, bounds, coefficients, or dimensions, and evaluate the child's admission tests. A parent-feasible primal point need not be child-feasible; for example, \(X_p=[0,1]\), \(X_v=[0,\tfrac12]\), and \(x_p=\tfrac34\). The solver may repair an inadmissible component using its declared initialization procedure or discard it and cold-start. Regardless of admission, every final status and certificate is verified against the current child QP using the same acceptance conditions as a cold solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map and validate inherited state against the child, repair or discard incompatible components, and apply unchanged final certification tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Child-Node Admission and Correctness

assumptions_latex: Related nodes use compatible variable and constraint identifiers.
The receiving solver declares which state components it can import.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w_p\text{ is reusable only through components whose identities and validity conditions remain defined for }P_v.

notation.meaning: Stored state from the parent or another related node.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reusable state exchanged between related search-node QP solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A search-tree QP warm start may contain a primal estimate, equality and inequality multiplier estimates, an active-set or basis estimate, barrier or scaling state, and symbolic or numerical linear-algebra metadata. Each component is associated with stable variable, row, and matrix identities. A child may import only components that can be mapped to its current formulation; unmapped rows, changed coefficients, incompatible dimensions, and stale numerical factors must be removed, reinitialized, updated by a validated procedure, or discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm-start state can include primal-dual, active-set, barrier, and factorization information, but every component must map validly to the current child formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Tree Warm-Start State
Search-Tree Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer and repair of parent QP state for a child-node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At child node \(v\), copy the parent state \(w_{ar v}=(x,y,\lambda,W,F)\), where \(W\) is an active-set estimate and \(F\) is reusable factorization metadata. Apply the child's new bounds and rows, project or otherwise repair \(x\) toward the child affine constraints, delete multipliers for removed rows, initialize multipliers for new rows to zero, and invalidate every factorization block whose matrix pattern or numerical values changed. Start the QP solver from the repaired state. If repair fails or residuals exceed warm-start admission thresholds, discard the affected state and use a cold initialization; final status tests remain identical to those of a cold solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Copy parent state, impose child modifications, repair primal-dual data, invalidate stale factors, and fall back to a cold start when admission tests fail.
assumptions_latex: The child relaxation differs from its parent through identified bound or row modifications.
Warm-start state components carry stable variable and constraint identifiers.
The solver defines finite admission thresholds for initial residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure supplies an admissible child initialization without allowing inherited state to weaken final certification requirements.

notation.meaning: Stored primal-dual and linear-algebra state at the parent node.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: parent-to-child state transfer with repair and stale-factor invalidation is a standard tree-search warm-start pattern

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches Search-Tree Warm Starts, but no cited source supports this particular transfer, repair, multiplier initialization, or factorization-invalidation procedure. The symbol w_{ar v} does not denote the parent consistently with the accompanying notation, and 'project or otherwise repair' is not a determinate algorithmic step. An authoritative search-tree QP warm-start source is required to select and state the exact procedure.

children.title: Relaxation Status Reporting
children.top_down_role: Termination, reliability, plus numerical-condition signals returned to the search controller.

assumptions_latex: The search controller discards a node only when a valid fathoming predicate has been verified.
A work limit, interruption, or numerical failure need not supply such a predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma\in\{\mathrm{limit},\mathrm{interrupted},\mathrm{numerical\ failure}\}\centernot\implies\text{node fathoming}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-tree safety boundary for nonconclusive relaxation termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reaching an iteration, time, or memory limit, or encountering a numerical failure, proves neither infeasibility nor bound dominance. Such termination may still return a separately verified feasible incumbent or valid bound, but the termination event itself cannot justify pruning. The node may be discarded only if an independently verified infeasibility, cutoff, exactness, or other valid fathoming certificate is also present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A limit or numerical failure is not a pruning certificate, although independently verified information obtained before termination can remain usable.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified Termination Cannot Justify Pruning

assumptions_latex: \(P_v\) is the current convex QP relaxation at node \(v\).
Every mathematical conclusion is checked using declared tolerances and the current data of \(P_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every definitive reported conclusion is paired with evidence sufficient to verify that conclusion for }P_v.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent semantics for a node-relaxation status and its accompanying evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relaxation report consists of a status \(\sigma\), termination metadata, achieved residuals, and any independently verified primal point, bound, or alternative certificate. Statuses may be refined by an implementation, but they must distinguish: (i) certified mathematical conclusions such as optimality, infeasibility, unboundedness, or a valid bound; (ii) provisional information such as an incumbent or bound that remains valid despite incomplete solution; and (iii) nonconclusive termination caused by a work limit, interruption, or numerical failure. A report may assert only the conclusions supported by its attached evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report termination separately from mathematical conclusions, and attach independently checkable evidence to every claimed optimizer, bound, infeasibility result, or unboundedness result.
knowledge_statements.title: Status Classes and Evidence Semantics
Relaxation Status Reporting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutually distinguishable statuses and evidence returned by a search-tree QP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A node solve returns exactly one status from \(\{\mathrm{optimal},\mathrm{lower\_bound},\mathrm{infeasible},\mathrm{unbounded},\mathrm{cutoff},\mathrm{limit},\mathrm{numerical\_failure}\}\), together with its evidence. Optimal requires a feasible primal point and accepted KKT residuals; lower-bound requires a verified dual bound; infeasible requires a valid alternative certificate; unbounded requires a verified feasible recession direction; and cutoff requires a certified lower bound meeting the incumbent cutoff. Limit and numerical-failure statuses carry achieved residuals and any independently valid incumbent or bound, but make no stronger claim. The search tree may prune only on infeasible, cutoff, or another status carrying an explicit pruning certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report one status with matching evidence, distinguish limits and numerical failures from mathematical conclusions, and permit pruning only when a valid certificate supports it.
assumptions_latex: The node relaxation is a convex QP in a minimization search tree.
Status-specific residual and certificate tolerances are declared before verification.
Any incumbent reported with a limited solve is checked for node feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each definitive status has an explicit verification predicate, while uncertified termination cannot by itself justify pruning.

notation.meaning: Termination with a certified bound but without a certified optimizer.
Certified proof that the node cannot improve the incumbent.
Termination caused by a declared work, iteration, or time budget.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tree-search correctness requires separating certificate-bearing mathematical statuses from resource and numerical terminations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A representation is appropriate for Relaxation Status Reporting, and separating certificate-bearing conclusions from resource or numerical termination matches the leaf. However, the exact seven-status taxonomy and its evidence obligations are uncited and are not universal across QP solvers or search-tree frameworks. A specific authoritative interface or solver-status locator is needed to establish this classification and the precise pruning semantics.
